title: Projectile Target Challenge: Pick Angle and Speed
description: A launcher sits at the left end of a flat 70 m field marked every 10 m. A flagged target zone with a gold disc stands down the field. Set the launch angle and speed, then press Launch: the orange ball flies along its arc and leaves a trail. The previous shot's arc stays as a faded grey path. Readouts give landing distance, miss, flight time, highest point, launches used and targets hit. Hit targets at 30 m, 45 m and 18 m within 10 launches.

game.objective: Hit three targets (30 m, then 45 m, then 18 m) by landing within 1.5 m of each centre, using no more than 10 launches.
game.hint: At the same speed, angles that add up to 90° (like 30° and 60°) land at the same distance, and 45° goes farthest. Doubling the speed makes the shot go four times as far.

assumptions: This is a simplified simulation: no air resistance, and the ball starts at ground level on flat ground.
Gravity is 9.8 m/s² straight down. The sideways speed stays constant; only the vertical speed changes.
Positions come exactly from the projectile formulas, so landing distance = speed² × sin(2 × angle) ÷ 9.8. The longest shot is about 63.8 m (25 m/s at 45°).
The ball is treated as a point (drawn large so it is visible; its path is drawn through its centre) and the flight ends when it returns to ground height.
A hit is a landing within 1.5 m of the target centre, both edges counted. Every flight plays over about 2 s on screen, so screen time differs from the flight-time readout.
Real balls are slowed by air and land shorter than shown, especially at high speed; the 45° best angle is exact only without air resistance.
